output:
I'll start by looking at the docs and package layout.

I've read all the code and docs. I'll apply the fixes now.

The shell call failed twice because its arguments were cut off. I'll make the edits with `edit_file` instead, starting with `lexer.py`.

Two of those edits failed with permission and busy errors. I'll check the current state of both files before retrying.

Now `interp.py`, `loader.py`, `report.py`, `data.py` and `convert.py`.

Next I'll rewrite the loader.

I'll edit the loader with `edit_file`.

The unit tests pass and the check tool is clean. I'll try some edge cases the unit tests might not cover.

I fixed the bugs in `/app/layercfg`, and the package now follows the docs. All 56 unit tests pass with `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. `python tools/check.py --data data` reports 0 broken on all 136 resolved configs. A full `run` over `/app/data` exits 0, writes 136 documents, and lists 14 configs in `errors.json` with the expected error classes.

I also resolved a small config I wrote in `/tmp` to try edge cases. It covered `250ms`, `1.5 KB`, list trimming, `#` handling, `$$` and `\$`, a template section, and a shared file's section not carrying over. All came out as the docs describe.

What I changed:
- **Syntax:**
  - The assignment separator is now whichever of `=` or `:` comes first.
  - Inline `#` comments only start after a space or tab.
  - `\$` in double-quoted values gives `$$`.
  - Whitespace stripping, section headers and `%include` lines use spaces and tabs only.
  - Files are read as raw bytes, so a stray carriage return is no longer turned into a line break.
- **Includes:**
  - After a shared file ends, the including file stays in its own section.
  - The include list has each file once, in first-read order.
  - A file still being applied can't be included again.
  - A config's own lines are all parsed before any `%include` is applied, so a syntax error beats an include error.
- **References:**
  - References are expanded after the merge, using each key's final value, instead of when each line is read.
  - Dotted references split at the last dot.
- **Output:** template sections (names starting with `_`) are no longer written or converted.
- **Types:**
  - `250ms` and similar durations now parse.
  - `KB`, `MB`, `GB` and `TB` are powers of 1000.
  - List items that are empty after trimming are dropped.

I wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`. I didn't touch `/app/tests`, `/app/data` or `/app/docs`.

One thing I left alone: `run` doesn't delete a stale `OUT/resolved/<id>.json` from an earlier run if that config now fails. The docs don't say to remove it.

command_result.command: cd /app && find . -type f -not -path './.git/*' | head -100 && cat docs/overview.md && wc -l layercfg/*.py docs/*
cd /app && cat docs/syntax.md docs/include.md docs/interp.md docs/types.md docs/output.md docs/changelog.md; ls docs/archive tools data | head -30
cd /app && for f in layercfg/*.py; do echo "=== $f"; cat $f; done
cd /app && sed -n 40,70p docs/include.md; cat docs/interp.md; sed -n 1,12p docs/types.md; cat docs/archive/*; cat layercfg/interp.py; sed -n 1,30p layercfg/lexer.py
cd /app && git status --short 2>&1 | head; ls -l layercfg; grep -n 'strip' layercfg/lexer.py layercfg/values.py
cd /app && python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -30; git diff --stat 2>&1|head -3; grep -n 'IsADirectory' layercfg/data.py; python tools/check.py --help 2>&1 | head
cd /app && python tools/check.py --data data 2>&1 | tail -30; rm -rf /tmp/o; python -m layercfg run --out /tmp/o; echo rc=$?; cat /tmp/o/errors.json | head -40; ls /tmp/o/resolved | wc -l

cd /tmp && rm -rf d && mkdir -p d/configs d/shared && cd d && printf '{"types":{"s.t":"duration","s.sz":"size","s.l":"list","*.n":"int"}}' > schema.json && printf '[S]
n = 1_000
t=250ms
sz = 1.5 KB
l = a, b,, c ,
c=#336
d = x # c
e: a=b
q = "\${HOME} $$ cost $5"
r = ${S.n}$$${n}
[_t]
z=${nope}
%%include a.conf
after=1
' > configs/x.conf && printf 'k=1
[other]
v=2
' > shared/a.conf && python -m layercfg resolve x --data . ; echo $?
cd /tmp/d && PYTHONPATH=/app python -m layercfg resolve x --data . ; echo $?
